title: AI tells -- the chat-assistant register
description: The chat-assistant voice that survived lexical patching. Each entry is a voice, not a word: synonym-swapping does not remove it. Per-model fingerprints inside this register drift fast, so treat model attributions as snapshots.

rules.name: Cut the intimacy performance
rules.message: faux candor: {match} -- cut the intimacy performance; candor is the unhedged claim

examples.bad: Let's be real: the gate is slow on a cold cache.
examples.good: The gate takes 12 s on a cold cache.

rules.fix: Delete the frame and make the claim it was protecting.

citation.note: Mechanizable core. tropes.fyi files this as "False Vulnerability". Judgement remainder in ai-tells-register.faux-candor-remainder, because the catalog's actual test is whether the vulnerability is risk-free, which no token carries. The structure catalog's "Here's the thing" overlaps -- that form is in ai-tells-structure.false-suspense-frames.

rules.name: Judge whether an admission carries risk
rules.message: faux candor: candor is the unhedged claim itself

match.question: Does this admission cost the author anything -- a named mistake, a measured failure, a refused feature -- or is it performed vulnerability with no exposure?

examples.bad: We're not perfect, and we're always learning.
examples.good: The 3.0 release shipped with a broken lockfile path for six days.

rules.fix: Replace the performance with the specific admission and its cost.

citation.note: Judgement remainder of ai-tells-register.faux-candor-core. The counter-signal catalog names the positive form: "a concrete anecdote or a mistake admitted with its cost".

rules.name: Drop the unearned intensifier
rules.message: intensifier tic: {match} -- drop it; add the specific claim that would justify it

examples.bad: The API is genuinely well designed.
examples.good: The API has four endpoints and one auth mode.

rules.fix: Delete the adverb and add the claim that would have justified it.

citation.note: Mechanizable core. tropes.fyi files these as "magic adverbs". `actually` is deliberately OMITTED from the token list despite the catalog naming it: it is a correct contrastive adverb in technical prose ("the flag actually reads the parent"), and prose-inflation.intensifier already owns the measured degree adverbs on the same reasoning. Judgement remainder in ai-tells-register.intensifier-tics-remainder.

rules.name: Judge whether emotion is announced or earned
rules.message: unearned emotion: add the specific claim, or drop the adverb

match.question: Is the reaction this adverb announces supported anywhere in the passage by a measurement, an example, or a named consequence?

examples.bad: The rewrite is remarkably clean.
examples.good: The rewrite deletes 400 lines and adds one function.

rules.fix: Supply the support, or delete the adverb.

rules.name: Delete the analysis wrapper and keep the noun
rules.message: analytic filler: {match} -- delete the wrapper; keep the noun

examples.bad: It's worth noting that, at its core, the loader is a cache.
examples.good: The loader caches resolved paths.

rules.fix: Delete the wrapper and keep the noun it packaged.

citation.note: Mechanizable core. `granular` is deliberately OMITTED even though the catalog names it: the immutable historical record at https://github.com/srobroek/slopvac/blob/18c37dcaf2d11ef43ab9cf4610cae0664e2644af/packages/slopvac-lint/docs/exclusions.md records that upstream ai-tells.OverusedVocabulary was disabled partly for flagging `granular`, which has an ordinary technical use. The remainder was retired 2026-09-22 after adjudication showed 16 percent precision. Overlaps upstream ai-tells.EmptyPadding, ai-tells.EmptyPaddingStacked, ai-tells.FillerPhrases, and ai-tells.LabelAndExplain, all of which stay enabled.

rules.name: Format only when the data has columns
rules.message: over-formatting: format only when the data has columns or the items are parallel and independent

match.question: Does each table, heading, and bold-colon bullet in this document carry data with real columns or items that are parallel AND independent, or would two sentences of prose say the same thing?

examples.bad:
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Purpose | It loads things |
examples.good: The loader reads the lockfile.

rules.fix: Unwrap the structure into prose where the items are neither columnar nor independent.

citation.note: A direct reward-model artifact, with per-model formatting fingerprints measured in https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.12150. Judgement-only at document scope: a table is correct or not depending on whether the data has columns, which is exactly the thing a pattern cannot see. The mechanizable slice of this entry is ai-tells-formatting.inline-header-list, which counts the bullet SHAPE. prose-format.prose-block is the inverse metric -- prose that should have been a table.

rules.name: Take the position the evidence supports
rules.message: hedged symmetry: take the position the evidence supports; cut the ballast

match.question: Is each counter-claim in this passage one somebody actually makes, or was it added so the passage reads even-handed?

examples.bad: Lockfiles help reproducibility, though some argue they add friction.
examples.good: The lockfile pins every transitive dependency.

rules.fix: Delete the invented counter-claim and state the position the evidence supports.

citation.note: Upstream ai-tells.FalseBalance attempts the phrase forms and stays enabled. The judgement is whether the counter-claim has a holder, which needs domain knowledge. Related to but distinct from prose-inflation.hedge-stack, which counts hedges on ONE claim; this counts claims balanced against each other.

rules.name: Delete the approval residue and audit the surrounding text
rules.message: sycophancy residue: {match} -- delete it, then audit the surrounding text

examples.bad: Great question! The loader reads the lockfile.
examples.good: The loader reads the lockfile.

rules.fix: Delete the phrase, then re-read the surrounding prose, which came from the same session.

citation.note: Enforced at every tier for the same reason ai-residue.chat-leakage is: it is session residue, never a register choice. Fully mechanizable as a token list, so no judgement partner; the catalog's own fix names the audit step, which is carried in `fix`. Overlaps upstream ai-tells.SycophancyMarkers, ai-tells.AffirmativeFormulas (kept at error even for source comments in .vale.ini), and ai-tells.ClosingPleasantries.

rules.name: State the judgement literally
rules.message: figurative verdict: {match} -- state the judgement literally, with the observation that supports it

examples.bad: The abstraction earns its keep.
examples.good: The abstraction removes three near-duplicate functions.

rules.fix: State the judgement as a claim, with the observation that supports it.

citation.note: Mechanizable core, as a literal token list. Distinctly 2026 register: the catalog records that it SURVIVED the lexical patching that killed the 2023-24 adjective bands, which is why it is worth a token list even though token lists decay. Upstream ships one rule per figurative verb -- ai-tells.FigurativeLands, FigurativeHolds, FigurativeQuiet, FigurativeCarries and twelve more -- all of which stay enabled, so expect duplicates. Judgement remainder in ai-tells-register.figurative-verb-verdict-remainder.

rules.name: Judge whether a metaphor carries a verdict with no evidence
rules.message: figurative verdict: the construction carries the verdict so no evidence has to

match.question: Does this sentence deliver a judgement through a metaphor while stating no observation that would let a reader disagree?

examples.bad: The design pays for itself.
examples.good: The design removes the second config file, so there is one place to look.

rules.fix: Replace the metaphor with the observation and the judgement it supports.

citation.note: Judgement remainder of ai-tells-register.figurative-verb-verdict-core, and the durable form: the catalog warns the specific verbs drift per model generation while the construction does not.

rules.name: Name what breaks, or drop the framing
rules.message: urgency inflation: {match} -- name what breaks if the reader ignores it, or drop the framing

tokens: the stakes have never been higher

examples.bad: The importance of the lockfile cannot be overstated.
examples.good: Without the lockfile, a transitive minor bump breaks the build.

rules.fix: Name the consequence, or delete the framing.

citation.note: Mechanizable core, enforced at every tier: .vale.ini already keeps upstream ai-tells.UrgencyInflation at error even for source comments, so this port inherits that disposition. Stakes asserted to substitute for consequence. Judgement remainder in ai-tells-register.urgency-inflation-remainder.

rules.name: Judge whether stakes name a consequence
rules.message: urgency inflation: name what breaks if the reader ignores it

match.question: Does this passage name what breaks if the reader ignores it, or only that the matter is urgent?

examples.bad: Getting this right is critical.
examples.good: A wrong value here silently skips every file.

rules.fix: State the failure mode, or delete the urgency.

rules.name: Say the choice was made, and why
rules.message: organic-consequence framing: {match} -- say the choice was made, and who made it

examples.bad: The single-config design falls out naturally.
examples.good: The maintainers chose one config file so there is one place to look.

rules.fix: Name the person who chose it and the constraint that drove the choice.

citation.note: Mechanizable core, enforced at every tier because it erases the agent who chose -- the same defect prose-agency.false-agency and prose-agency.agentless-passive gate at error in every register. Upstream ai-tells.OrganicConsequence covers this and stays enabled. Judgement remainder in ai-tells-register.organic-consequence-remainder.

rules.name: Judge whether a design is presented as self-caused
rules.message: organic-consequence framing: a designed decision presented as something that happened

match.question: Did a person choose the thing this sentence describes as arising on its own?

examples.bad: The threshold settles at 34 words.
examples.good: The maintainers set the threshold at 34 words after measuring 30 and 32.

rules.fix: Name the chooser and the reason.

rules.name: Judge whether an abstraction occupies the subject slot
rules.message: false agency: name the human, or use "you" and put the reader in the seat

match.question: Is the subject performing deliberate intent or choice, or is it a checkable technical actor under a specification? If it is a MUST/MUST NOT/DEFAULT line, imperative steering, quoted text, or a component causally operating, PRESERVE; flag only unowned intent, merit, or self-causation.

examples.bad: The complaint becomes a fix.
examples.good: The team fixed it that week.

examples.bad: A bet lives or dies in days.
examples.good: You learn within a week whether the bet paid.

examples.bad: The parser rejects malformed JSON.
examples.note: preserve: technical actor performing a checkable operation

examples.bad: The cache evicts entries.
examples.note: preserve: component performing a checkable operation

examples.bad: MUST reject invalid input.
Run the migration.
The cache wants to protect you.
examples.good: The cache evicts entries.

rules.fix: Name the human. Where no specific person fits, use "you" and put the reader in the seat.

citation.note: Judgement remainder of prose-agency.false-agency, which mechanises the seven named subject-verb bands. This rule carries the open case, because the catalog's own definition -- "an abstraction promoted to actor" -- is productive: any abstract noun can occupy the subject slot, so no closed list finishes the job. The catalog distinguishes it from the two entries around it: those grant a component desert ("earns its keep", ai-tells-register.anthropomorphised-justification-core) or self-causation ("falls out naturally", ai-tells-register.organic-consequence-core). An artifact that disclaims a claim ("this change makes no claim about...") is ai-tells-register.disclaimed-claim-core, not this rule.

rules.name: State the measured property, not the desert
rules.message: anthropomorphised justification: {match} -- state the measured property

examples.bad: The lookbehind is load-bearing.
examples.good: Removing the lookbehind adds five false positives per README.

rules.fix: State the measured property that would justify the claim.

citation.note: Mechanizable core. Upstream ai-tells.AnthropomorphicJustification covers this and stays enabled. BROADER than the content-shape anthropomorphism entry, which covers subjects ACTING and is mechanised as prose-agency.anthropomorphism; this covers subjects DESERVING. Judgement remainder in ai-tells-register.anthropomorphised-justification-remainder.

rules.name: Judge whether a component is granted intent
rules.message: anthropomorphised justification: a component granted intent so its value needs no argument

match.question: Does this sentence assert a component's value by granting it merit rather than by naming a property a reader could check?

examples.bad: The cache more than repays its complexity.
examples.good: The cache removes one network round trip per run.

rules.fix: Replace the merit claim with the checkable property.

rules.name: Say what was checked, not what the artifact claims
rules.message: disclaimed claim: {match} -- say who checked what, or that nobody did

examples.bad: This configuration change makes no claim about endpoint health.
examples.good: This branch does not check endpoint health.

examples.bad: Publication does not establish that the server launches on every host.
examples.good: This branch does not test whether the server launches.

examples.bad: Keep the IaC server configured without claiming it manages the same resources.
examples.good: Keep the IaC server configured. It cannot delete stacks directly.

examples.bad: The brief has no links, so this description cannot independently verify the results.
examples.good: The brief has no links, and nobody reran these checks.

rules.fix: Name the check and its result, such as "This branch does not test X", or delete the sentence.

citation.source: Slopvac adversarial review of a change-communication draft (2026-10)
citation.note: Mechanizable core. An artifact -- a change, a publication, registry metadata, the description itself -- is made the subject of an epistemic verb in a negated disclaimer, so the sentence reports what the artifact does not claim instead of what anybody checked. All four bad examples come from one model-written merge-request draft and its blind rewrite; the review that missed them filed the first under ai-tells-register.false-agency-remainder. The verb list is the epistemic one only. `makes no guarantee` and `does not guarantee that` state a component contract ("the queue does not guarantee that jobs run in order"), and `does not prove that` and `does not imply that` state what a signal means ("lint does not prove that a statement is correct", "a 200 response does not imply that the write committed"); the remainder judges those. Judgement remainder in ai-tells-register.disclaimed-claim-remainder.

rules.name: Judge whether an artifact disclaims instead of a check being named
rules.message: disclaimed claim: say who checked what, or that nobody did

match.question: Does this sentence make an artifact disclaim a claim or a proof, instead of naming who did or did not check what?

examples.bad: The registry metadata is not evidence that the package installs.
examples.good: Nobody has installed the package from the registry yet.

examples.bad: These results should not be read as confirming browser support.
examples.good: This branch runs no browser tests.

examples.bad: The queue does not guarantee that jobs run in order.
examples.note: preserve: a component contract, not an artifact disclaiming a claim

rules.fix: Name the check and its result, such as "This branch does not test X", or delete the sentence.

citation.source: Slopvac adversarial review of a change-communication draft (2026-10)
citation.note: Judgement remainder of ai-tells-register.disclaimed-claim-core. It covers the paraphrases no fixed verb list reaches, such as "is not evidence that" or "should not be read as confirming".
